kb.t: What types of chatbots do you build?
kb.k: types type kind kinds of chatbot rule based rag retrieval flow decision tree hybrid llm ai all which type only ai not only ai categories
kb.a: All the main types, and I pick the right one for your job: 1) Rule-based — keyword/pattern matching to pre-written answers; fast, cheap, predictable, no hallucinations. 2) AI/LLM-based — a model like Claude or GPT generates replies; flexible, understands natural language, billed per call. 3) Retrieval (RAG) — searches your knowledge base then answers from what it finds; grounded in your real data. 4) Flow / decision-tree — a guided step-by-step script where the user picks options (order forms, bookings, risk calculators). 5) Hybrid — rules handle common cases, AI handles the rest with rules as a fallback. My live bots already cover all of these — for example the WhatsApp Trading FAQ bot is rule-based with an optional AI mentor (hybrid), and the Instagram restaurant bot is AI with a rule-based fallback.

kb.t: What is rule-based vs AI, and which do I need?
kb.k: rule based rules deterministic vs ai difference predictable keyword matching fallback which one hybrid
kb.a: Rule-based answers are fast, predictable and free to generate — great for known FAQs. AI handles open-ended questions in natural language. Alex often combines them: rules for the common cases, AI for the rest, with rules as a fallback so the bot never goes silent. He'll recommend the right mix for your use case.
